meta.name: Cisco CCST Cybersecurity (100-160)
meta.notes: Initial pack — CCST Cybersecurity 100-160 covering Essential Security Principles, Basic Network Security Concepts, Endpoint Security Concepts, Vulnerability Assessment/Risk Management, and Incident Handling.

questions.question: Your organisation classifies data as Public, Internal, Confidential and Restricted, and each level has different handling rules. Which pillar of the CIA triad does this classification scheme primarily protect?
options: Availability (systems remain reachable when needed)
Confidentiality (data is disclosed only to authorised parties)
Integrity (data is not altered without authorisation)
Non-repudiation (an actor cannot deny having performed an action)
questions.explanation: Data classification is used to decide who may read, copy or transmit each piece of information, so it primarily enforces confidentiality — the assurance that data is only disclosed to authorised parties. Availability is about systems staying reachable (backups, redundancy), integrity is about detecting or preventing unauthorised change (hashing, digital signatures), and non-repudiation ties an action to a specific actor (signed audit logs, digital signatures) rather than restricting who can see the data.

questions.question: A helpdesk employee gets a phone call from someone claiming to be a senior IT manager who urgently needs their password reset because they are locked out before a board meeting. Which type of attack is the caller most likely attempting?
options: SQL injection (malicious input aimed at a database)
ARP poisoning (redirecting traffic on a local segment)
Social engineering — specifically pretexting (impersonating a role to build a false story)
Man-in-the-middle attack (silently relaying and possibly altering traffic)
questions.explanation: The attacker is building a fabricated scenario (a locked-out executive under time pressure) and impersonating a role of authority to trick a human into breaking process. That is textbook pretexting, a form of social engineering. SQL injection targets database input fields, ARP poisoning manipulates layer-2 address mappings on a LAN, and a man-in-the-middle attack relays traffic between two parties — none of them describe a phone call aimed at a helpdesk operator.

questions.question: You want to place a segment between the untrusted internet and the internal LAN that hosts only public-facing services (web server, mail relay, reverse proxy), so that a compromise there cannot pivot straight into the internal network. What is this segment called?
options: A demilitarised zone (DMZ) reachable from the internet and firewalled from the LAN
A virtual private network (VPN) tunnel between two sites
A guest wireless SSID isolated on its own VLAN
A honeynet built from deliberately vulnerable decoy hosts
questions.explanation: A DMZ is a segmented network placed between the internet and the internal LAN specifically to host services that must be reachable from outside; both perimeter and internal firewall rules restrict what can move between the three zones, so a breach of the public server does not automatically expose the internal network. A VPN provides encrypted transport between endpoints, a guest SSID isolates untrusted client Wi-Fi, and a honeynet is a decoy network used to observe attackers rather than to serve production traffic.

questions.question: A security policy requires that a stolen or lost laptop must not expose company data even if the attacker removes the drive and reads it on another machine. Which control most directly satisfies this requirement?
options: Enable a screen-saver password after 5 minutes of inactivity
Turn on full-disk encryption such as BitLocker or FileVault
Install anti-malware software with real-time scanning
Enforce a 15-character passphrase on the local user account
questions.explanation: Full-disk encryption keeps the contents of the drive unreadable without the decryption key, so pulling the disk out of the laptop and mounting it in another machine still yields ciphertext. Screen-saver passwords and stronger local passphrases only guard the running OS session — they are bypassed once the drive is removed. Anti-malware protects against malicious code executing on the endpoint, not against offline access to files.

questions.question: During vulnerability triage you see a CVE with a CVSS base score of 9.8, marked Critical. Which statement best describes what the CVSS base score actually tells you?
options: The intrinsic severity of the vulnerability itself (exploitability + impact), independent of your environment and any temporary factors
A ranking based on how frequently this specific CVE has been observed in the wild during the last 30 days
The financial cost, in US dollars, that a successful exploitation would incur for a typical enterprise
The exact patch priority for your organisation, taking into account your compensating controls and asset value
questions.explanation: The CVSS base score captures the intrinsic characteristics of the vulnerability — attack vector, complexity, required privileges, and confidentiality/integrity/availability impact — and stays constant over time and across environments. Real-world exploitation frequency is reflected in the separate Temporal metrics (and in threat feeds such as CISA KEV), monetary loss is not part of the CVSS model at all, and organisation-specific priority is what the Environmental metrics adjust once you overlay your asset value and controls.

questions.question: Your security team wants to reduce the blast radius of stolen credentials so that a leaked password alone cannot let an attacker sign in as a user. Which control most directly addresses that requirement?
options: Rotate the password every 30 days regardless of any signal
Increase the account lockout threshold to 20 failed attempts before locking
Store all passwords in a shared spreadsheet protected by a single team password
Require multi-factor authentication (MFA) at sign-in using a second factor such as an authenticator app or FIDO2 key
questions.explanation: Multi-factor authentication requires the user to present something they know (the password) plus at least one additional factor they have or are (a code from an authenticator app, a hardware key, a biometric). Even if the password is phished or reused from a breach, the attacker cannot complete sign-in without the second factor. Rotating passwords slows persistence but does nothing about a freshly stolen credential, raising the lockout threshold actually makes brute-force easier, and shared credential spreadsheets multiply the risk instead of reducing it.

questions.question: An analyst wants to see the exact sequence of packets exchanged between a client and a suspicious server, including TCP flags and payload, so they can decide whether the flow was malicious. Which tool is best suited to that job?
options: nmap — an active network port scanner and service fingerprinter
iptables — a Linux kernel packet-filtering framework
Cisco Umbrella — a cloud-delivered DNS-layer security service
Wireshark — a packet capture and protocol analyser
questions.explanation: Wireshark captures packets from a network interface (or reads a pcap) and decodes them protocol by protocol, so an analyst can inspect the three-way handshake, TLS handshake, HTTP requests, or raw bytes. nmap probes hosts for open ports and running services rather than capturing existing traffic, iptables filters packets in the Linux kernel but does not decode payloads for analysis, and Umbrella enforces policy on DNS queries in the cloud without exposing packet-level detail.

questions.question: A user reports a ransom note on their workstation and files with unfamiliar extensions. Which action should the on-call responder take FIRST, before deeper investigation or restoration?
options: Format the hard drive to remove all traces of the ransomware immediately
Pay the ransom in cryptocurrency to recover the files as quickly as possible
Isolate the affected workstation from the network (disable Wi-Fi, unplug Ethernet) to stop lateral spread
Post a screenshot of the ransom note in the company chat so everyone is aware
questions.explanation: The immediate priority in an incident is containment: cutting the infected host off the network stops the ransomware from encrypting shares or reaching other endpoints while responders gather evidence. Wiping the disk destroys the forensic evidence needed to understand the intrusion, paying the ransom is discouraged (no guarantee of decryption, funds criminal activity, and may violate sanctions), and broadcasting the note publicly leaks incident detail and can panic users without protecting anything.

questions.question: Which of the following data flows correctly matches a common protocol with the default TCP port a firewall rule would need to allow?
options: SSH — TCP port 21 for encrypted remote shell sessions
HTTPS — TCP port 443 for TLS-encrypted web traffic
SMTP — TCP port 143 for outbound mail transfer between servers
RDP — TCP port 22 for Windows remote desktop sessions
questions.explanation: HTTPS runs over TLS on TCP/443 by default — that is the port a boundary firewall must permit outbound (or inbound to a web server) to allow encrypted web traffic. SSH uses TCP/22 rather than 21 (which is FTP control), SMTP relaying between mail servers uses TCP/25 (with 587 for authenticated submission) — not 143, which is IMAP for retrieval — and RDP listens on TCP/3389, not TCP/22.

questions.question: You are drafting a corporate password policy. Recent NIST SP 800-63B guidance favours which of these practices for user-chosen passwords?
options: Force a password change every 30 days regardless of any compromise signal
Ban password managers so that users must memorise every credential individually
Require the password to include exactly one uppercase, one digit and one symbol, with a hard maximum length of 12 characters
Require at least 8 characters, screen new passwords against a list of common or breached passwords, and only rotate on evidence of compromise
questions.explanation: Modern NIST guidance (SP 800-63B) recommends a reasonable minimum length (at least 8 characters, with longer allowed and encouraged), checking new passwords against known-breached and common-password lists, and rotating only when there is evidence of compromise — periodic mandatory rotation nudges users toward predictable, weaker variants. Blocking password managers reduces password quality, and prescriptive composition rules combined with a low maximum length shrink the effective search space and frustrate users into risky habits.
